People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying as easy as sending a message. NPCI launched it in 2016, and it moves money straight from your bank account to anyone using a phone number, a UPI ID or a QR scan. You don't need a card, cash or a slow bank transfer.

The shift picked up speed once small shops, vegetable sellers and auto drivers began showing a QR code. When almost everyone you pay accepts it, carrying cash feels like extra work. Apps like PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm also made sign-up quick, often just a few minutes.

The three main reasons:

Speed and simplicity: Payments go through in seconds, at any hour, including holidays.
Low or no cost: Paying friends and most shops is free for users, so there's little reason to avoid it.
Works everywhere: One app links all major banks and works from big malls to roadside stalls, even on basic smartphones.

Together, these make UPI the easy default, and habits follow convenience.
